one_month_reasoning: The window holds Q3 2026 results on Oct 28 before the open [3]. Guidance is $0.70-0.71 post-split against consensus of about $0.72 [2,4], so a beat is the expected outcome and the Q4 guide is the swing factor. The Oct 28 FOMC decision lands the same afternoon: Kalshi has hold 73% and a 25bp hike 28%, on about $2M+ of volume [23]. Hyperscaler Q3 capex prints come in the last week of October. The supervisor verified my earnings-day reaction history: +3.6%, -12.2% (a beat that sold off), +3.2%, and +4.5% then +6.3% the next day [17]. That is three up and one large down, so the downside is asymmetric if the guide disappoints. Zacks's Sep 28 downgrade on valuation [28] shows the bar is high. I model a near-symmetric fat-tailed distribution: 75% weight on sigma 10.5% and 25% on sigma 19% for a gap move, with a +0.6% drift for upward estimate revisions and momentum. The result is P(>=85.67) of 0.52, essentially unchanged from round 1 and in line with the group.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 2028E EPS $3.65 x 24.5x forward P/E = $89.4 (weight 0.5); (b) trailing EPS at Oct-2027 of $3.05 x 29x = $88.5 (weight 0.3); (c) peer-set base-rate drift of +7% from $85.67 = $91.7 (weight 0.2). Blend = $89.6, rounded to $89.5.

bear.story: AI capex digestion as 2028 capex growth slows to +6-12% [26,27]. Datacom orders roll over from a 1.23 book-to-bill [1], Foxconn Interconnect takes the Kyber midplane [24], and the Fed hikes through the winter [23]. 2028E EPS is cut to about $2.9 and the multiple goes to about 20x, the hardware median plus a premium [8]. The stock falls about 32%, around the peer-set 5th-10th percentile [21]. A recession is now a smaller part of this case: Kalshi has 21% for 2027 [22], down from the thin Polymarket 35% I used in round 1.

base.story: Hyperscaler capex reaches $1.0-1.2T in 2027 [13,26] and EPS tracks consensus ($3.29 for 2027) with modest beats. The multiple compresses from about 26x to 24.5x forward as the market looks to slower 2028 growth and a hiking Fed. EPS growth roughly offsets the de-rating, for a gain of about 4%.

bull.story: Beat-and-raise continues (2027 EPS went from $2.86 to $3.29 in 90 days [4]) and 2028E EPS reaches about $4.1. APH keeps its Kyber/Rubin content, or the GF report proves wrong, and a ~29x multiple holds. The stock beats the analyst high target ($115) [5]. Peer base rates show a fat right tail: the pooled p75 is +44% and p90 +93% [21].

thesis_break_reason: A close below about $60 (-30%) would break the closing floor that held twice in 2026 ($59.58 on Mar 30 and $59.60 on May 19; intraday low $59.01) [17]. At about 18x 2027 consensus EPS it would be near the hardware-sector median [8] and the low end of the 10-yr P/E range [7]. It is also beyond the peer-set 10th percentile drawdown after a strong year [21]. Getting there almost certainly needs estimate cuts (datacom book-to-bill below 1, a hyperscaler capex cut, or a confirmed loss of Kyber share [24]), not multiple drift alone. I moved it from $62 to $60 after the supervisor's check of the double bottom: $62 sat inside the noise of that floor.

reasoning: Round 2 changes are small and mostly left-tail and multiple related. (1) Base rates: as the supervisor asked, I recomputed the conditional base rate on 18 connector, component and EMS peers [21]. After a +25-60% year the pooled median 12m forward total return is +13.5%, with 33% negative, p10 -26% and p5 -37% (long-history subset: median +9%, 35% negative). That confirms APH's own +23% median was survivor-inflated, but my round-1 haircut to +8% already sat below the peer median, so the drift method barely changes (+7%). Disagreement with the supervisor: the peer base rate implies P(close >= today) of about 0.60-0.65 before valuation. I go below it to 0.55 because APH trades at 41x TTM, near the top of its 10-yr range [7], and because of the Kyber and rate risks below. I do not go to 0.515: I see no evidence that a 41x multiple on a stock still getting upward revisions makes a loss more likely than a gain. (2) The GF Securities report on Foxconn Interconnect and Kyber [24,25], which I missed, adds content risk inside the horizon (Rubin Ultra), so I trim 2028E EPS by about 1% and add left-tail mass. (3) Macro odds: I replaced the thin Polymarket recession market (35%, ~$10k volume) with Kalshi's liquid 2027 recession contract at 21% [22]. That lowers recession weight, but Kalshi's Fed markets show a 70% chance of a December hike and 40% for January [23], so I cut the forward multiple to 24.5x and the trailing one to 29x. (4) On 2028 capex growth I accept the supervisor's resolution (Goldman +12%, UBS +6%) and use 12% EPS growth. Fair value falls from $92 to $89.5. The mixture is bear 22% at $58 (sigma 0.26), base 52% at $89 (0.17) and bull 26% at $120 (0.22), with the tails smoothed slightly fatter to match the peer base-rate spread (pooled sdlog 0.43; APH's own 0.25). It gives a median of about $89.5, a mean of about $92, P(>=86) of 0.55 (from 0.58) and P(<60) of 0.14. Research limits: the GF report's date could not be confirmed (MSN would not render and Intellectia returned 403), and Kalshi was read through its public API.
